title: Plimpton 322: Babylonian table of Pythagorean triples
summary: A clay tablet whose rows each relate to a whole-number triple fitting a squared plus b squared equals c squared, more than a thousand years before Pythagoras.
why: Shows advanced Babylonian mathematics; most surviving Babylonian maths tablets date from 1800-1600 BCE.

notes.problem: Overstates the table: source says 'Each row of the table relates to a Pythagorean triple'; the tablet does not list all three numbers of each triple.
